passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following discussion and analysis contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the federal securities laws and should be read in conjunction with the disclosures we make concerning risks and other factors that may affect our business and operating results. You should read this information in conjunction with the Consolidated Financial Statements and the notes thereto included in Part II, Item 8., of this Annual Report on Form 10-K . See also “Forward-Looking Statements” immediately prior to Part I, Item 1., of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. For management’s discussion of our consolidated results for the year ended June 27, 2025 in comparison with the combined results for the year ended June 28, 2024, and other financial information related to fiscal year 2025, refer to Part II, Item 7., “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations,” included in our 2025 Annual Report on Form 10-K, filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”) on August 21, 2025. Unless otherwise indicated or the context requires, references herein to specific years and quarters are to our fiscal years and fiscal quarters. As used herein, the terms “we,” “us,” “our,” and the “Company” refer to Sandisk Corporation and its subsidiaries. Overview Our Business Sandisk is a leading global semiconductor memory company with more than 30 years of innovation in NAND flash technology. We are a vertically integrated solutions provider with ownership of chip-level design and IP, front and back-end manufacturing, as well as systems engineering and design. With a differentiated innovation engine driving advancements in storage and semiconductor technologies, our broad and ever-expanding portfolio delivers powerful flash storage solutions for artificial intelligence (“AI”) workloads in datacenters, edge devices, and consumer applications. Our technologies enable everyone from students, gamers, and home offices to the largest enterprises and public clouds to produce, analyze, and store data. Our solutions include a broad range of solid-state drives (“SSDs”), embedded products, removable cards, universal serial bus drives and wafers and components. Our broad portfolio of technology and products addresses multiple end markets of “Datacenter” (formerly referred to as “Cloud”), “Edge” (formerly referred to as “Client”), and “Consumer.” The Datacenter end market is comprised primarily of products for datacenters, cloud service providers, and private cloud customers. Through the Edge end market, we provide our original equipment manufacturer (“OEM”) and channel customers a broad array of high-performance flash solutions across personal computer, mobile, gaming, automotive, physical AI, at-home entertainment, and industrial spaces. The Consumer end market is highlighted by our broad range of retail and other end-user products, which capitalize on the strength of our product brand recognition and vast presence around the world. A total of $2,879 million and $692 million of our cash and cash equivalents were held outside of the U.S. as of July 3, 2026 and June 27, 2025, respectively. There are no material tax consequences that were not previously accrued for the repatriation of this cash. Our cash equivalents are primarily invested in money market funds that invest in U.S. Treasury securities and U.S. Government agency securities. Operating Activities Net cash provided by operating activities primarily consists of net income or loss, adjusted for non-cash charges, plus or minus changes in operating assets and liabilities. Net cash used as a result of changes in operating assets and liabilities was $212 million for 2026, compared to $380 million net cash provided for 2025 and to $86 million net cash provided for 2024, reflecting an increase in the volume of our business, as discussed above. Changes in our operating assets and liabilities are largely affected by our working capital requirements, which are dependent on the volume of our business and the effective management of our cash conversion cycle as well as timing of payments for taxes. Our cash conversion cycle measures how quickly we can convert our products into cash through sales. Changes in days in inventory, or DIO, are generally related to the timing of inventory builds. Changes in days payable outstanding, or DPO, are generally related to production volume and the timing of purchases during the period. From time to time, we modify the timing of payments to our vendors. We make modifications primarily to manage our vendor relationships and to manage our cash flows, including our cash balances. Generally, we make payment term modifications through negotiations with our vendors or by granting to, or receiving from, our vendors’ payment term accommodations. In 2026, DSO decreased 3 days when compared to the prior year, primarily due to the timing of shipments and continued strong receivables collections. DIO increased 43 days over the prior year, primarily due to inventory builds to meet demand. DPO increased 14 days over the prior year, primarily due to routine variations in the timing of purchases and payments. credit_strengths.text: Sandisk's operating cash flow and free cash flow are substantial, reflecting a vertically integrated NAND flash franchise serving datacenter, edge and consumer markets. The company converted a large share of revenue into cash, and its cash balance exceeds reported borrowings, producing a net cash position. This liquidity provides a strong buffer against the cyclical memory sector.

The debt note shows the term loan and revolver fully repaid, leaving no reported borrowings. Interest coverage is exceptionally high, and the current ratio exceeds the sector median, indicating ample short-term liquidity. The indicative financial risk profile is Minimal, with leverage and cash-flow tiers at the lowest risk level.

key_risks.text: The risk-factor passage discloses that a material portion of cash and cash equivalents is held outside the U.S. While no material tax consequences were unaccrued, repatriation could still be constrained by local regulations or tax costs. This geographic cash concentration may limit flexibility for debt service or shareholder returns if domestic liquidity needs arise.

The debt note describes a prior term loan and revolver secured by substantially all assets, with a leverage covenant solely for the revolver. Although now repaid, the facility's restrictive covenants on indebtedness, liens, dividends and investments could constrain future financing or distributions if redrawn. The company's history of a large distribution to WDC highlights potential shareholder-return pressure.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: With no reported borrowings, debt service is minimal. Interest coverage is far above the sector median, and free cash flow is more than sufficient to cover any future interest. The company's net cash position and strong operating cash flow provide substantial capacity to absorb a cyclical downturn or fund growth initiatives without external financing.

Operating cash flow covers capital expenditures many times over, and the cash conversion cycle lengthened due to inventory builds, which could pressure liquidity if demand softens. Nevertheless, the absence of debt and large cash balance mean debt servicing capacity remains robust. Future leverage could rise if the company funds shareholder returns or acquisitions with new borrowings.

overall_credit_view.text: Sandisk presents a minimal credit risk profile, with no reported debt, net cash, and very high interest coverage. The company's strong operating cash flow and free cash flow generation, coupled with a safe Altman Z-score, support a stable credit outlook. The main credit considerations are the cyclical nature of NAND flash and potential shifts in capital allocation.

Analyst judgement: the company's leverage sits well below the sector median, and its profitability metrics are top-decile. However, the absence of debt maturities and a history of large distributions to a former parent suggest that future leverage could increase. We would monitor any new financing, shareholder returns, or working capital swings that could erode the current net cash position.

credit_strengths.text: Sandisk的營運現金流及自由現金流均相當可觀，反映其垂直整合的NAND快閃記憶體業務服務數據中心、邊緣及消費市場。該公司將大部分收入轉化為現金，且其現金結餘超過所呈報借款，產生淨現金狀況。此流動性為應對週期性記憶體行業提供了強大緩衝。
債務附註顯示定期貸款及循環信貸已悉數償還，並無所呈報借款。利息覆蓋率極高，且流動比率超過行業中位數，顯示短期流動性充裕。指示性財務風險狀況為極低，槓桿及現金流級別均處於最低風險水平。

key_risks.text: 風險因素章節披露，現金及現金等價物的重大部分持有於美國境外。儘管並無重大稅務後果未計提，匯回資金仍可能受當地法規或稅務成本限制。此地理上的現金集中可能限制償債或股東回報的靈活性，倘國內流動性需求出現。
債務附註描述先前以絕大部分資產作抵押的定期貸款及循環信貸，槓桿契約僅適用於循環信貸。儘管現已償還，該融資對債務、留置權、股息及投資的限制性契約，倘重新提取，可能限制未來融資或分派。該公司曾向WDC作出大額分派的歷史，凸顯潛在股東回報壓力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 由於並無所呈報借款，償債金額極少。利息覆蓋率遠高於行業中位數，且自由現金流足以覆蓋任何未來利息。該公司的淨現金狀況及強勁營運現金流，提供雄厚能力以吸納週期性低迷或撥付增長計劃，而無需外部融資。
營運現金流覆蓋資本開支多倍，且現金轉換週期因庫存增加而延長，倘需求減弱可能對流動性構成壓力。儘管如此，並無債務及龐大現金結餘意味償債能力仍然穩健。倘該公司以新借款撥付股東回報或收購，未來槓桿可能上升。

overall_credit_view.text: Sandisk呈現極低信貸風險狀況，並無所呈報債務、淨現金及極高利息覆蓋率。該公司強勁的營運現金流及自由現金流產生，加上安全的Altman Z-score，支持穩定信貸展望。主要信貸考量為NAND快閃記憶體的週期性及資本配置的潛在轉變。
分析師判斷：該公司槓桿遠低於行業中位數，且其盈利能力指標處於最高十分位。然而，並無債務到期及曾向前母公司作出大額分派的歷史，顯示未來槓桿可能增加。我們將監察任何新融資、股東回報或營運資金波動，這些可能侵蝕當前淨現金狀況。
